about: The featured moments of "the world at a moment", and what this project can say about each region at each of them. An entry either POINTS AT one of the map’s own dated anchors, or is a sourced entry from the pass of 2026-11-27, or states that nobody has looked, or states a finding about the record itself.
rules: Part B rules: real sources, a tier on every claim, nothing typed without a source. A sourced entry here is NOT added to the map’s 565 anchors: that is an approved set and growing it is its own ruling.
regions: North Africa and the Near East

moments.title: The crucifixion
moments.why: An execution almost every scholar accepts happened, on a year nobody can fix: 30 and 33 CE both fit Pilate’s prefecture and the gospels’ own calendar notes. THE TIER IS ABOUT THE DATE, NOT THE EVENT.

Oceania.finding: The settled record pauses here, and that is a measured result rather than a gap in our reading.
Oceania.detail: West Polynesia is settled by c. 800 BCE and then nothing moves east for about eighteen hundred years. At this moment the Pacific frontier is where it was eight centuries ago.
Oceania.shownDate: the pause: c. 800 BCE to c. 1025 CE
Oceania.source: Wilmshurst, J.M., Hunt, T.L., Lipo, C.P. & Anderson, A.J., “High-precision radiocarbon dating shows recent and rapid initial human colonization of East Polynesia”, PNAS 108, 2011, 1815–1820 — 1,434 dates from at least 45 islands. Migration into East Polynesia begins only after a 1,800-year PAUSE following the settlement of Samoa c. 800 BC, in two phases: the Society Islands c. 1025–1120 CE, the rest c. 1190–1290 CE. Mulrooney et al., PNAS 108, 2011, E192, dispute the statistics while accepting the late chronology. MICRONESIA IS EARLIER: this map’s own Nan Madol anchor is 900 CE.

Europe.label: Rome under Tiberius
Europe.source: Tiberius, Roman emperor 14–37 CE (Encyclopædia Britannica). The reign is among the best-attested facts of the period, and the panel treats it as such.
Europe.note: The prefect who tried the case answers to this emperor, which is the only reason the year can be argued at all.

North Africa and the Near East.label: Parthia under Artabanus II
North Africa and the Near East.source: Artabanus II of Parthia, r. c. 12–38/40 CE. The regnal dates are reconstructed from coins and from Tacitus and Josephus, and scholars differ by several years at both ends, so the tier is contested.
North Africa and the Near East.note: The empire between Rome and India, and the regnal dates are reconstructed rather than recorded.

South Asia.label: Kujula Kadphises founds the Kushan empire
South Asia.source: Kujula Kadphises, founder of the Kushan empire, reign estimated c. 25–85 CE. THE CHRONOLOGY IS UNSETTLED: the Rabatak inscription fixes the dynasty’s genealogy but not its absolute dates, and the start of the Kanishka era is placed at 127 CE on Harry Falk’s work or at 78 CE on the older view, which is still argued (Sino-Platonic Papers 227, 2012).
South Asia.note: Begram and the Kabul valley. The dynasty is certain and its absolute chronology is argued over a fifty-year range.

East Asia.label: The Han restored, the capital at Luoyang
East Asia.source: Guangwu, who restored the Han in 25 CE and moved the capital to Luoyang, r. 25–57 CE (Encyclopædia Britannica).
East Asia.note: Guangwu takes the throne in 25 CE and moves the capital east. The empire at the other end of Eurasia from Tiberius.

moments.title: The Younger Dryas begins
moments.why: An abrupt return to near-glacial cold, dated in the Greenland ice cores. Göbekli Tepe’s world is on the far side of it.

Migration into East Polynesia begins only after a 1,800-year PAUSE following the settlement of Samoa c. 800 BC, in two phases: the Society Islands c. 1025–1120 CE, the rest c. 1190–1290 CE. Mulrooney et al., PNAS 108, 2011, E192, dispute the statistics while accepting the late chronology. MICRONESIA IS EARLIER: this map’s own Nan Madol anchor is 900 CE.
